_doc: M&A and material debt issuance events for hospital muni obligors, 2023-Q1 through 2025-Q1. Focus: 4 known false negatives of covenant tripwire (Adventist Health W. Coast, NCH, Lompoc Valley, ProMedica) + 23-name BBB+ pilot universe.
methodology: WebSearch + WebFetch across Bond Buyer, Becker's, Healthcare Dive, Fierce Healthcare, Modern Healthcare, rating agency releases, hospital IR pages. Leverage_impact judgment: HIGH = downgrade-triggering or >25% debt increase; MEDIUM = material capital outlay but absorbable; LOW = small bolt-on; NONE = no M&A in window.

confidence_legend.HIGH: Two or more independent sources, dollar figures consistent
confidence_legend.MEDIUM: Single authoritative source or some figures inferred
confidence_legend.LOW: Inferred from context; not verbatim cited

ma_events.counterparty: Tenet Healthcare — Sierra Vista Regional Medical Center + Twin Cities Community Hospital (CA Central Coast), plus physician practices and imaging centers
ma_events.rationale: Acquire 2 California Central Coast hospitals; closed April 1, 2024. Deal also included Revenue Cycle Services partnership with Tenet's Conifer.
ma_events.citation_text: Adventist Health closed its acquisition of two Tenet Healthcare hospitals on the central California coast on April 1, 2024. The hospitals were purchased for approximately $550 million (after-tax proceeds of approximately $450 million). For the year ended December 31, 2023, the two hospitals and related operations generated revenues of approximately $337 million.

ma_events.counterparty: Series 2024 revenue bonds (CA municipal)
ma_events.rationale: Funded Tenet acquisition; Fitch downgraded IDR to BBB+ from A on the issuance citing ~31% leverage increase.
ma_events.citation_text: On May 1, Fitch downgraded Roseville, Calif.-based Adventist Health's issuer default rating to 'BBB+' from 'A,' primarily driven by the significant increase in leverage (about 31%) Adventist is taking on to support the acquisition. Long-term debt is expected to increase by about $750 million once the deal closes.

Adventist Health (West Coast)._notes: FN #1 CONFIRMED — Tenet acquisition is the unambiguous downgrade driver. $750M debt add on ~$5.8B revenue base = ~13% revenue-relative debt step. Fitch attribution explicit. Acquisition added $337M revenue at deal close but $750M debt = 2.2x revenue multiple on debt-to-acquired-revenue.

ma_events.counterparty: Self-funded capital program — Patty and Jay Baker Pavilion (80k sqft orthopedic facility) + R.M. Schulze Family Heart and Stroke Critical Care Center
ma_events.rationale: Slower-than-expected margin improvement combined with high leverage from ongoing capital build-out (multiple new pavilions targeting March 2025 completion). NOT an M&A event — pure operational + capital-spend driven downgrade.
ma_events.citation_text: Fitch Ratings downgraded NCH Healthcare System's issuer default rating to BBB-plus from A-minus, citing weak operating results, limited internally generated cashflow, high leverage and ongoing capital needs. Moody's also downgraded to Baa1 from A3.

Naples Comprehensive Health (NCH)._notes: FN #2 — NO M&A DRIVER FOUND. OhioHealth acquisition rumor is unsubstantiated by search (OhioHealth operates in Ohio; geographic implausibility). Downgrade was operational: weak margins + leveraged capital plan (orthopedic pavilion + heart/stroke center). This is a covenant-tripwire MISS that pure M&A-watching would also miss; need a separate capital-program leverage screen.

ma_events.counterparty: Internal capital program — Lompoc Health Village Center ($8M, primary care expansion in Vandenberg Village) + ongoing remodeling/expansion
ma_events.rationale: Moody's cited narrowing liquidity from cash funding of capital needs. Small standalone hospital district with limited scale; no acquisitions.
ma_events.citation_text: Lompoc Valley Medical Center's rating was downgraded to 'Baa1' from 'A3' by Moody's, driven by the system's narrowing liquidity that resulted primarily from cash funding of its capital needs. As of June 30, 2023, the District has recorded $2,619,238 as construction-in-progress.

Lompoc Valley Medical Center._notes: FN #3 — NO M&A DRIVER. Pure liquidity/scale issue — small CA hospital district burning cash on small capex projects with no offsetting M&A. Confirms initial hypothesis: 'small standalone hospital scale issues' was correct. Future-tripwire add: cash-funded capex as % of unrestricted cash.

ma_events.counterparty: Welltower / HCR ManorCare unwind (multi-year process)
ma_events.rationale: Fitch downgrade BB+ to BB- May 9, 2023 (NOT 2024 as initially recorded), placed on Rating Watch Negative. Fitch cited 'precipitous decline in liquidity in fiscal 2022' from HCR ManorCare senior care segment losses, NOT M&A leverage. Multi-year process of exiting/restructuring senior care business follows.
ma_events.citation_text: Fitch Ratings cut the system's rating two notches to BB-minus from BB-plus on $1.8 billion of outstanding bonds sold in 2015 and 2018... 'reflects the precipitous decline in liquidity in fiscal 2022, which has placed significant pressure on an already weak balance sheet and leaves the organization with very little flexibility should management's financial improvement plan not materialize fully.'

ma_events.counterparty: ProMedica Senior Care sale (multiple counterparties)
ma_events.rationale: Asset sale program subsequently de-levered ProMedica and led to $1.8B in bonds being removed from negative watch following the sale.
ma_events.citation_text: $1.8B in ProMedica bonds taken off negative watch following sale

ProMedica Health System._notes: FN #4 — NO ACQUISITION DRIVER. Downgrade was the tail of the disastrous 2018 HCR ManorCare/Welltower JV — senior-care segment liquidity bleed, NOT new M&A. Date was May 2023 (not 2024). Moody's subsequently upgraded ProMedica to Baa3 from Ba1 in Dec 2025 as divestitures completed. Covenant tripwire missed this because the leverage event was 5 years old and the downgrade was a delayed cash-flow consequence.

ma_events.counterparty: Henry Ford Health — 8 SE Michigan hospitals + Genesys + addiction treatment facility contributed to JV
ma_events.rationale: Closed Sept 30, 2024; launched Oct 1, 2024. Ascension contributed 8 Michigan hospitals into JV controlled by Henry Ford Health (retains Detroit HQ, branding, CEO). Ascension is divesting/contributing, not acquiring — leverage-decreasing for Ascension parent, leverage-neutral to slightly negative for the JV vehicle.
ma_events.citation_text: Henry Ford Health and Ascension Michigan closed their proposed joint venture on September 30 and launched their newly combined organization on October 1, 2024. The combined organization employs approximately 50,000 team members. The deal created a $10.5 billion organization. Following the close, Ascension was left with just four operated hospitals in Michigan.

Ascension Health._notes: JV is contribution-out for Ascension (de-leveraging at parent). Burden falls on Henry Ford Health credit. The deal value is the combined revenue base, not cash consideration.

ma_events.counterparty: Ascension Michigan — receiving 8 hospitals + addiction facility
ma_events.rationale: Henry Ford absorbs 8 Ascension Michigan hospitals into combined organization; retains HQ, CEO, branding. This is leverage-increasing for Henry Ford as it absorbs operational responsibility for previously-Ascension assets.
ma_events.citation_text: The combined organization employs approximately 50,000 team members at more than 550 sites across Michigan. The arrangement brought eight southeast Michigan hospitals and an addiction treatment facility from Ascension Michigan and Ascension Genesys Health System under the Henry Ford Health umbrella.

Henry Ford Health._notes: Not in original 24-name BBB+ pilot, but flagged because it's the counterparty to a major event. Worth adding to watchlist.

UPMC._notes: No material M&A identified in window 2023-Q1 to 2025-Q1. Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh acquisition was 2001, not recent. UPMC has been an acquirer of Ohio Trinity Health System (CommonSpirit divestiture) but that closed later in 2025 — outside window. Searches returned only historical info.

ma_events.counterparty: CommonSpirit Health — remaining 50% stake in MercyOne (Iowa, 16 medical centers, 400+ sites of care)
ma_events.rationale: Trinity acquired CommonSpirit's remaining stake in MercyOne, becoming sole parent. Trinity already owned 50%; this was a buyout consolidation, not a new acquisition of operations.
ma_events.citation_text: Trinity Health, one of America's largest Catholic health systems, has completed the acquisition of MercyOne, based in Iowa. Trinity Health and CommonSpirit Health announced they have signed an agreement for Trinity Health to acquire all facilities and assets of MercyOne. With the deal, Trinity Health acquires MercyOne's 16 medical centers and more than 400 sites of care.

Trinity Health._notes: Buyout of existing JV partner — economically low-leverage-impact since Trinity already consolidated MercyOne in financials.

Cleveland Clinic._notes: No material M&A in window. Cleveland Clinic CEO has publicly discussed M&A appetite but no announced deals 2023-Q1 to 2025-Q1. Indian River/Martin Health deals were 2019. Capital spending on London hospital and international growth, but not US M&A.

ma_events.counterparty: Trinity Health — sold 50% MercyOne (Iowa) stake
ma_events.rationale: De-consolidation of MercyOne. Net leverage-reducing for CommonSpirit.
ma_events.citation_text: Trinity Health to Acquire CommonSpirit Health's Share of MercyOne Health System, Become Sole Parent

ma_events.counterparty: Series 2024 taxable + CA + CO revenue bonds
ma_events.rationale: Refinancing + ~$500M net new money for reimbursement of prior capex ($300M) and future capex ($200M). Refunded $700M of 2019 series + $250M of Dignity 2014A. Total debt ~$18.4B inclusive of issue.
ma_events.citation_text: Proceeds from the series 2024 bonds, along with expected premium, will go toward refinancing certain debt outstanding... and will provide about $500 million of net new money that will be used to reimburse prior capital spending (about $300 million) and fund future expenditures ($200 million). Total debt outstanding, inclusive of the Series 2024 bonds, is approximately $18.4 billion.

CommonSpirit Health._notes: Continued routine capital-program refinancing post-CHI/Dignity. Net new money only $500M on $35B revenue base = immaterial. Fitch reaffirmed A stable. Not a leverage event.

ma_events.counterparty: Brown University — academic affiliation agreement, rebrand to Brown University Health, $150M Brown contribution over 7 years
ma_events.rationale: Rebrand + financial commitment, NOT a merger. Brown emphasized 'two organizations remain separate and independent.' Lifespan-Care New England merger application filed (Hospital Conversion Act) separately — pending regulatory.
ma_events.citation_text: Beginning July 1, 2024, Brown will make annual contributions of $15 million to $25 million — totaling $150 million over seven years — to support the mission of Lifespan.

Brown University Health (Lifespan)._notes: Inflow of capital from Brown — leverage-positive for Lifespan/Brown University Health. Care New England merger remains in regulatory review; previously rejected in 2022, so substantial execution risk.

ma_events.counterparty: Steward Health Care (bankruptcy) — Good Samaritan Medical Center (Brockton) + St. Elizabeth's Hospital (Brighton)
ma_events.rationale: Distressed acquisition from Steward bankruptcy estate. BMC purchased Good Samaritan outright; took over operations of St. Elizabeth's (property remained with Apollo as mortgage holder). Approved by bankruptcy court Sept 4, 2024; closed October 2024. Subsequent Globe coverage (Feb 2026) says these acquired hospitals have been 'dragging down' BMC.
ma_events.citation_text: Boston Medical Center (BMC) signed an asset purchase agreement to acquire and operate Good Samaritan Hospital in Brockton. Additionally, BMC and Steward reached an agreement to transfer the operations of St. Elizabeth's to BMC. The sale price was $140 million. Boston Medical Center took over the former St. Elizabeth's Hospital in Brighton and Good Samaritan Medical Center in Brockton in October 2024.

Boston Medical Center._notes: MATERIAL — $140M deal value on $2.5B revenue base = 5.6%, but operational drag from distressed assets is the real leverage risk. Boston Globe Feb 2026 retrospective explicitly says acquired Steward hospitals have hurt BMC. Worth watching for downgrade catalysts in 2025-2026.

ma_events.counterparty: Northwell Health (acquirer)
ma_events.rationale: Announced Feb 2024; closed May 7, 2025 (outside our window). Northwell pledged $1B investment into Nuvance facilities over 5 years.
ma_events.citation_text: Northwell and Nuvance first announced their intention to come together in February 2024. The merged organization now operates 28 hospitals... with a unified system boasting $22.6 billion in revenue. Northwell has pledged to invest $1 billion into Nuvance's facilities over the next five years.

Nuvance Health._notes: Announcement was in-window; closing was just outside (May 7, 2025). Nuvance is being absorbed — credit profile becomes Northwell's. Leverage at Northwell now applies.

ma_events.counterparty: KentuckyOne Health — Jewish Hospital + Louisville-area assets, 5,500 employees
ma_events.rationale: Completion of multi-year acquisition initiated in 2019; final closing October 2024. State and foundation support involved. Jewish Hospital rebranded as UofL Hospital - Jewish Campus.
ma_events.citation_text: In October 2024, UofL assumed KentuckyOne Health's Louisville assets. Some 5,500 former KentuckyOne employees joined UofL and UofL Health. Jewish Hospital and UofL Hospital became one united hospital with two locations.

ma_events.counterparty: $144M UofL Hospital tower expansion
ma_events.rationale: Seven-story tower expansion adding 360 private beds + 20 ORs + 24-bed observation unit.
ma_events.citation_text: A new seven-story tower anchoring a $144 million expansion and upgrade to UofL Hospital was announced.

UofL Health._notes: Both M&A (KentuckyOne) AND capital expansion — meaningful leverage event. Worth monitoring for downgrade catalysts.

ma_events.counterparty: Atlantic Health System (signed definitive agreement)
ma_events.rationale: Definitive merger agreement signed June 2024 (announced Jan 2024). Combined system would have exceeded $5B revenue. SUBSEQUENTLY CANCELLED October 2025 — outside our window. During window, deal was active.
ma_events.citation_text: The two New Jersey-based health systems first announced plans to combine in January 2024 and signed a definitive agreement to merge in June 2024. The combined nonprofit systems would have exceeded $5 billion in annual revenue.

Saint Peter's Healthcare System._notes: Deal was pending during window; cancellation came post-window (Oct 2025). No closed M&A or debt event in 2023-Q1 to 2025-Q1.

ma_events.counterparty: WoodBridge Healthcare (terminated) / StoneBridge ($706M offer rejected)
ma_events.rationale: Tower remained independent after rejecting $706M offer (Dec 2023) and later having WoodBridge deal terminated (Nov 2024). Subsequently laid off 350 employees and closed Pottstown ICU/cancer/endoscopy units.
ma_events.citation_text: In December 2023, the nonprofit WoodBridge Inc. was expected to send Tower Health a non-binding agreement for the purchase of all of Tower's assets for $706 million. However, Tower Health rejected a $706 million offer. A previously announced divestiture to WoodBridge Healthcare, Inc. was terminated in November 2024.

Tower Health._notes: Distressed system — failed sale attempts and continued operational deterioration. Already deep speculative-grade. Service closures (Pottstown ICU/cancer/endoscopy) mid-2024 likely covenant-relevant.

Atrium Health / Advocate Health._notes: Atrium-Advocate Aurora merger closed December 2022 — JUST before our window begins (2023-Q1). Per terms, neither side guaranteed the other's debt. Integration ongoing through window but no new M&A or major debt events identified. Note: deal was structurally lever-light because debt remained separate at sub-credit level.

ma_events.counterparty: Highmark Health funded $1B Allegheny General transformation (cardiovascular tower + ED) — 10-year program
ma_events.rationale: $1B Highmark capital injection for AGH modernization. Tower construction begins early 2025, opens 2030. 100+ inpatient beds + cardiovascular ICU.
ma_events.citation_text: Highmark Health, the parent company of Allegheny Health Network, is putting $1 billion into a decade-long transformation project for Allegheny General Hospital in Pittsburgh. The construction of the new cardiovascular tower is expected to begin in early 2025 and they plan to have the facility opened by 2030.

AHN / Allegheny Health Network._notes: Funded by parent Highmark Health (insurer) — different credit silo. AHN obligor leverage impact depends on JV/funding structure. Heritage Valley affiliation came Oct 2025 (outside window).

ma_events.counterparty: CSCDA Series 2024 bonds — $1.23B+ tax-exempt + taxable
ma_events.rationale: CSCDA issued $1,235,890,000 in tax-exempt and taxable bonds for LLUMC for medical facility improvements and refunding prior debt. Total LLUMC outstanding debt ~$1.7B.
ma_events.citation_text: In 2024, the California Statewide Communities Development Authority (CSCDA) issued bonds to finance improvements to LLUMC's medical facilities as well as refund a portion of prior issued bonds. The Medical Center had approximately $1.7 billion of outstanding debt.

Loma Linda University Medical Center._notes: Mostly refunding existing $883M issuance (the original Troesh Medical Campus bonds) but Fitch UPGRADED LLUMC to BB+ from BB on new campus' solid operating performance. So leverage event is operating-neutral to positive.

Frederick Health Hospital._notes: No material M&A identified in window. Opened New Market Medical Center (primary care joint venture with Frederick Primary Care Associates) Sept 2024 — small bolt-on, not material. FY24 financials available on Maryland HSCRC site.

Mount Sinai NYC._notes: No material M&A in window. Beth Israel closure announced (closed April 2025 — outside window). UnitedHealthcare network dispute Jan 2024 was operational, not transactional.

Memorial Hermann (Houston)._notes: No material M&A in window. Prior Baylor Scott & White $14B merger cancelled Feb 2019. No new deals 2023-2025-Q1.

Houston Methodist._notes: No material M&A in window. New tower on TMC campus mentioned but pre-existing build.

ma_events.counterparty: Kettering Reproductive Health (small bolt-on)
ma_events.rationale: Small specialty practice acquisition, not material. UC Health's bigger story is $256M accumulated operating losses 2021-2023 and S&P debt rating downgrade due to operating losses.
ma_events.citation_text: UC Health Acquires Kettering Reproductive Health

UC Health Cincinnati._notes: Operational distress (not M&A) is the credit story — $256M accumulated losses; awaiting $279M Medicaid supplemental payment to plug the hole. S&P downgrade was operational.

Hurley Medical Center._notes: No material M&A in window. Outreach Laboratory Services sale to Quest was 2018 (pre-window).

Mosaic Life Care._notes: No material M&A in window. Plaza 4 medical office building completion 2024 — small capex. Oracle Fusion ERP selection Oct 2024 — IT only.

ma_events.counterparty: Mountain Health Network + Marshall Health + Marshall University — combined to form Marshall Health Network (4 hospitals)
ma_events.rationale: Marshall Health Network formed via combination including 303-bed Cabell Huntington Hospital. Restructuring of existing affiliated entities rather than new acquisition.
ma_events.citation_text: Huntington-based Mountain Health Network, Marshall Health and Marshall University completed a combination to form Marshall Health Network, which consists of physician practices and facilities as well as four hospitals including the 303-bed Cabell Huntington Hospital.

Cabell Huntington Hospital._notes: Internal restructuring of already-affiliated entities, not net new acquisition. Likely leverage-neutral.

OU Health._notes: No material M&A in window. 2021 merger of OU Medicine + UOK College of Medicine faculty practice completed integration in Jan 2023 — pre-window. No new transactions 2023-Q1 to 2025-Q1.

obligors_with_material_ma_in_window: Adventist Health (West Coast) — HIGH: Tenet $550M acquisition + $750M debt
Boston Medical Center — HIGH: Steward $140M distressed acquisition
Nuvance Health — MEDIUM: Northwell merger announcement (closed post-window)
UofL Health — MEDIUM: KentuckyOne acquisition + $144M expansion
Ascension/Henry Ford — Henry Ford absorbed 8 Ascension MI hospitals via JV
Trinity Health — MercyOne consolidation (low impact, JV buyout)

fn_diagnosis.1_adventist_health_west_coast: M&A DRIVER CONFIRMED — Tenet acquisition, $750M debt add. Covenant tripwire missed this because it was a large refundable debt issuance + bolt-on acquisition, not a covenant breach. Should be catchable by debt-issuance-velocity screen.
fn_diagnosis.2_nch_naples: NO M&A DRIVER — pure operational + capital-program leverage. Multiple new pavilions self-funded. Need separate screen for capex-to-cash ratio.
fn_diagnosis.3_lompoc_valley: NO M&A DRIVER — small standalone hospital district funding capex from cash, narrowing liquidity. Need scale-floor + liquidity-ratio screen.
fn_diagnosis.4_promedica: NO NEW M&A DRIVER — downgrade was tail of 2018 HCR ManorCare/Welltower mistake. Senior care segment bleeding cash. Date was May 2023, not 2024. Need a 'legacy M&A unwind' watchlist.

summary.implication_for_tripwire: M&A-watching would have caught Adventist (1 of 4 FNs). The other 3 require: (a) capex-funded-by-cash velocity screen, (b) liquidity-erosion screen for small standalone hospitals, (c) legacy-deal-cleanup watchlist for systems with prior big strategic misadventures. Pure M&A leverage screen ~25% recall on this FN set.
